status_note: A bug in the documentation's text, minor. On main (35a2cb73, 2026-11-04) `nan_min` names numpy's `nanmin` (Expr and Series), so the wrong name is fixed there; the reason in both `nan_max` and `nan_min` is unchanged. No matching issue found on pola-rs/polars (2026-11-04); #17513 (open) is about `max`/`min` and NaN on length-1 groups.
summary: The documentation of `Expr.nan_min` and `Series.nan_min` (https://docs.pola.rs/api/python/stable/reference/expressions/api/polars.Expr.nan_min.html, py-polars/src/polars/expr/expr.py#L3751 and py-polars/src/polars/series/series.py#L2316 at py-2.1.0) says "This differs from numpy's `nanmax` as numpy defaults to propagating NaN values, whereas polars defaults to ignoring them." It should name `nanmin`. In both `nan_max` and `nan_min` the reason describes numpy's `max`/`min`, which propagate NaN, while numpy's `nanmax`/`nanmin` ignore NaN, the opposite of what the sentence attributes to them.
repro: Text only. py-polars/src/polars/expr/expr.py at py-2.1.0, `nan_min`: "This differs from numpy's `nanmax` as numpy defaults to propagating NaN values, whereas polars defaults to ignoring them." numpy: `np.nanmin([1.0, np.nan])` is 1.0 and `np.min([1.0, np.nan])` is nan.
handling: Nothing to work around: sverify follows the engine's behaviour, which the facts record. The fix is in Polars's documentation. Suggested wording: "This matches numpy's `min`, which propagates NaN; Polars's `min` ignores NaN, as numpy's `nanmin` does."
found_by: the Polars characterization reverse pass (2026-11-04): the docstrings and user guide at py-2.1.0 checked against each open fact

checked.note: Docstrings at py-2.1.0 (expr.py `nan_max` and `nan_min` both say `nanmax`). Main at 35a2cb73: expr.py and series.py say `nanmax` in `nan_max` and `nanmin` in `nan_min`, with the same reason. Duplicate search for "nan_min docstring nanmax": only #17513 (related).
